references.text: The prohibition against worshipping or serving other gods is founded in the second commandment, where God forbids idolatry.
Moses repeats the command to tear down altars, break sacred pillars, and destroy idols when the Israelites enter the land.
The same command to tear down altars, break sacred pillars, and burn up the Asherah poles of the peoples in the land.
Warning against serving the gods of the nations, for it would become a snare for Israel.
God repeats the command to tear down altars and break sacred pillars, and forbids worship of other gods.
Command to drive out the inhabitants and destroy all their cast images and high places.
Prohibition against setting up sacred pillars, which the Lord hates.
King Hezekiah removed the high places, broke the sacred pillars, and cut down the Asherah pole in obedience to this commandment.
King Josiah cleansed Judah and Jerusalem by tearing down altars and breaking sacred pillars and carved images.
Jesus rejects Satan's temptation by quoting that one must worship and serve only the Lord, which is the core of this commandment.
Clear allusion to and confirmation of the prohibition against mentioning or serving the names of foreign gods.
Thematic parallel regarding the necessity of breaking idols and destroying high places, even though the direction (judgment on Israel versus conquest) differs.
Prophetic fulfillment where God Himself carries out the cleansing from stone pillars that Israel was first commanded to do.
